new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word, where the phonological word includes any enclitics (so an enclitic shifts the stress rightward).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = the phonological word, explicitly 'word + enclitics if any'; data are tape-recorded Dolap (Pura) narratives, i.e. connected speech rather than citation forms. The statement is about Blagar as Steinhauer defines it (Pura, NE Pantar, Tereweng island); no Tereweng-island data are cited. The only Tereweng-specific data on prominence, Stokhof 1975 list 14 (p. 42), marks penultimate prominence in many words but final prominence in many disyllables (lap'a, nan'a, ar'u, mih'iŋ, is'iŋ, nɔw'ar..), so a penultimate rule is not confirmed for Tereweng itself.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is about Blagar of Dolap (Pura island) = blag1240 (LexiRumah pura1258), not about Tereweng-island speech. It applies to Tereweng only in the sense that Steinhauer (1977: 38; 1991: 177) and Stokhof (1975: 14) count Tereweng as a dialect of the Blagar language; Glottolog 5.1 and ISO (twg) treat Tereweng as a separate language under the Blagar node. No source describes Tereweng phonology first-hand. The only Tereweng-specific prominence data (Stokhof 1975, list 14, p. 42) show both penultimate and final prominence, so the 'always penult' rule is unverified for Tereweng. Reviewer should decide whether the catalog accepts an author-defined language-level statement for a Glottolog dialect-level split; if not, Tereweng has no stress statement.
